Implemented on branch `iam-titan-f10f`, commit `92c47154586` (Change-Id `I434df308687c03cbe456693954ba3363ed1e9cec`).

## Codebase AC evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Titan ARN listed in `bedrock_converse` | `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` added to the resource list |
| Both Claude ARNs retained | foundation-model `anthropic.claude-*` and inference-profile `*.anthropic.claude-*` both present, unmodified |
| Exactly one statement | one `statement {` block in `data.aws_iam_policy_document.bedrock_converse` |
| Actions unchanged | `bedrock:InvokeModel`, `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` — byte-identical |
| sid no longer Claude-only | `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly` → `InvokeScopedBedrockModels` |
| header comment corrected | no longer says "Claude-only" or "constraining the Anthropic model"; now names both families |
| `bedrock-ci-oidc.md:130` unchanged | not in the diff; sole hunk is `@@ -145,2 +145,4 @@` plus a one-phrase fix at `:32` |
| `bedrock-ci-oidc.md:239` unchanged | not in the diff; content intact, shifted +2 lines by the `:145` hunk |
| `:145` no longer claims "verbatim in shape" | rewritten to "the same shape ... which additionally grants the `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` embedding ARN that external CI does not need" |
| ADR no longer says "exactly two resource ARNs" | deployment-precondition section rewritten |
| `terraform validate` | **exit 0** — "Success! The configuration is valid." |
| `terraform fmt -check -recursive` | **exit 0** |
| no `src/rebar/` file modified | `git diff --name-only \| grep ^src/rebar/` → empty |

## Scope added during implementation

A whole-tree sweep for the claims this change falsifies — rather than editing only the cited lines — found three more in `infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md` that my own change made false:

- `:40` "you have not shown the **Claude-only scope** binds" → "the scoped model list binds"
- `:120` heading "a **non-Claude** model must be DENIED" → "an **unlisted** model must be DENIED"
- `:129` "the policy is meant to permit `anthropic.claude-*` **only**" → names both admitted families, and notes `amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` is in neither so the negative control still holds

The documented negative control still works unchanged: it probes `amazon.nova-pro-v1:0`, which the widened policy still denies.

`bedrock-access.md` was added to `file_impact`. I verified empirically that this does **not** void the plan-review attestation — `review-plan --status` returned `ok: true, verdict: certified, currency_basis: file_impact` both before and after the edit. The signed manifest carries its dep set frozen at signing; a path added later is not in it.

The three remaining "Claude-only" mentions in `bedrock-ci-oidc.md` (`:32`, `:160`, `:305`) describe the **external-CI** OIDC role, whose grant was *not* widened. They are correct as written. `:32` had said "the same Claude-only grant", which became false once the two policies diverged; reworded to "a Claude-only Bedrock grant of the same shape".

## Honesty note carried into the artifacts

Both the ADR and the commit message state that the grant is **declared, not confirmed live**: bug `1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38` records that `iam_s7.tf` has not been verified as applied, and a policy simulator cannot settle it because Converse authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel` while the distinct `bedrock:Converse` action simulates as denied.

## Remaining

The `[non-codebase]` AC — an operator applying the Terraform and attesting the Titan call succeeds from the instance role — is outstanding and cannot be met from this session. `make verify` has not yet run on this branch (deferred to avoid contending with the `47c8` verify on the same host).
